messages.subject: I think there is an error in SAX (PAA in fact)
messages.subject_clean: I think there is an error in SAX (PAA in fact)
messages.body_plain:
Hi folks:

I have accidentally bumped into an issue with SAX transform when testing my own code. It turns out that PAA in seewave is done wrong -- instead of cautiously accounting for unevenly broken segments it shortcuts to averaging their length, I believe... Here is an example:

library(seewave)
library(matlab) # for "reshape"

# data
x=c(-1, -2, -1, 0, 2, 1, 1, 0)
plot(x,type="l")
points(x,pch=16,lwd=5)
#segments
abline(v=c(1,1+7/3,1+7/3*2,8),lty=3,lwd=2)

# PAA implementation in seewave
l <- length(x)
PAA_number = 3
PAA <- array(0, PAA_number)
for (i in 1:PAA_number) {
  PAA[i] <- mean(x[round((i - 1) * l/PAA_number + 1):round(i * l/PAA_number)])
  print(paste("segment",i,"[",      # a debug output
              round((i - 1) * l/PAA_number + 1),
              ":",round(i * l/PAA_number),"] ->",
              PAA[i]))
}
points(x=seq(1+7/6,8,by=7/3),y=PAA,pch=3,lwd=3,col="red")

# PAA variant
paa <- function(ts, ap){
  len <- ncol(ts)
  res <- ts
  if(len != ap){
    if( (len %% ap) == 0 ){
      res <- reshape(ts, len %/% ap, ap)
    }else{
      tmp <- matrix(rep(ts,ap),byrow=T,nrow=ap)
      res <- reshape(tmp, len, ap)
    }
  }
  matrix(colMeans(res), nrow=1, ncol=ap)
}
paa1=paa(t(x),3)
points(x=seq(1+7/6,8,by=7/3),y=paa1,pch=3,lwd=5,col="blue")

# difference
paa1-t(PAA)

Thanks!

 <https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/-gD2OhCoHBw4/VgzqlSbg8LI/AAAAAAAAB3w/9OXjNzO7wmc/s1600/Rplot.png>

messages.subject: Spectral entropy with spec
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

Just to clear things up
In the documentation the spectral entropy sh is compute with "y = relative amplitude of the i frequency," (with sum(yi)=1).
But in the examples, for instance:

a<-synth(f=8000,d=1,cf=2000,plot <http://inside-r.org/r-doc/graphics/plot>=FALSE)
speca<-spec(a,f=8000,at=0.5,plot <http://inside-r.org/r-doc/graphics/plot>=FALSE)
##########################
# Shannon spectral entropy
##########################
sh(speca)

I don't see how the spectrum is normalized. So, the sum of the bin does not equal 1. Does it ?

Could you please clarify that point?
Thanks a lot.

P.G.
